profile.summary: DGRNA is a pretrained RNA language model built for long RNA sequences. It is built mainly from bidirectional Mamba2 layers rather than the Transformer layers of earlier RNA language models, a choice the authors make to handle long sequences efficiently, and was trained on about 100 million RNA sequences from the MARS database. Given RNA sequences, the released code returns a per-position representation that can be used for downstream tasks.

summary_quotes.text: Current RNA large language models are primarily based on Transformer architecture, which cannot efficiently process long RNA sequences, while the Mamba architecture can effectively alleviates the quadratic complexity associated with Transformers.
we propose a large foundational model DGRNA based on the bidirectional Mamba trained on 100 million RNA sequences
Pre-training is conducted on approximately processed 100 million RNA sequences derived from MARS database.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Tokens are embedded and passed through pairs of Mamba2 blocks: one reads the sequence forwards and one reads it reversed. A linear layer merges each pair's outputs. After the last pair, one multi-head attention layer with 32 heads and rotary embeddings is applied, followed by a final normalisation. The paper describes 12 bidirectional Mamba2 blocks, an output embedding of 768 dimensions per position and 100 million parameters. Pretraining is masked language modelling as in BERT: 15% of nucleotide tokens are corrupted and the model learns to recover them. Sequences are tokenised one nucleotide at a time, with T replaced by U and [CLS] and [EOS] tokens added at the ends. The model is built on the ESM and Fairseq code bases and uses an ESM-1b style alphabet. The released forward pass returns the hidden states, not token logits.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pretrained checkpoint is released, as a single file named checkpoint_best_100M.pt in a Google Drive folder. The README loads it through the function rna_mamba2_L24. The checkpoint has no version tag or hash in the sources read, so a result should name the repository commit and the file name. This page read commit 9f3513f6.

facts.value: Pretrained RNA language model (foundation model) using bidirectional Mamba2 layers.

quotes.text: DGRNA: RNA foundation model with bidirectional mamba2-attention
we propose a large foundational model DGRNA based on the bidirectional Mamba trained on 100 million RNA sequences

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Embedding layer, then paired forward and reverse Mamba2 blocks merged by a linear layer at each depth, then one multi-head attention layer with 32 heads and rotary embeddings, then a final norm. The paper gives 12 bidirectional Mamba2 blocks and a 768-dimensional output. The paper's Methods say both "1 attention heads" and, for the final Flash Attention layer, 32 attention heads; the released code uses 32.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A batch of named RNA sequences as strings, converted to tokens by the model's batch converter. The README example includes N and gap characters in one sequence. The paper tokenises single nucleotides after replacing T with U, with a 16-symbol set that includes ambiguity codes, N and '-', and adds [CLS] and [EOS] tokens.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: About 100 million RNA sequences randomly selected from the MARS database. MARS combines sequences from RNAcentral, MG-RAST, the Genome Warehouse, MGnify and NCBI nt. The authors collected 1.7 billion sequences, removed redundancy with MMseqs to 1.2 billion, and kept sequences longer than 3 and shorter than 2048 before sampling.

Finally, we obtained 1.2 billion non- redundant RNA sequence[35, 36]. We keep RNA sequences longer than 3 and shorter than 2048, randomly selected to obtain a total of approximately 100 million RNA sequences

strengths.text: The authors chose Mamba layers to avoid the quadratic cost of Transformer attention, so the design targets long RNA sequences.

quotes.text: the Mamba architecture can effectively alleviates the quadratic complexity associated with Transformers

strengths.text: Each layer reads the sequence in both directions, so every position's representation uses context on both sides.
The authors report in the preprint abstract that DGRNA performed better than existing RNA language models on six downstream tasks.

quotes.text: which has demonstrated exceptional performance across six RNA downstream tasks compared to existing RNA language models

limitations.text: GPU only. The README says only GPU is supported, and the code depends on Triton, causal-conv1d, mamba-ssm and flash attention.

quotes.text: Note that currently only GPU is supported

limitations.text: The weights are a manual download from Google Drive with no stated licence. If the file is missing from the torch hub folder, the loader tries a fallback URL on the RNA-FM project server, which is not the DGRNA checkpoint source named in the README.
The README lists dependency versions but gives no install command.
At 100 million parameters, DGRNA is smaller than most RNA language models, as the authors themselves note.

quotes.text: Currently DGRNA only has 100 million parameters, which is fewer than most RNA language models.

gaps: The paper does not date the MARS download used for training.

The checkpoint configuration was not opened, so the paper's 12 bidirectional blocks and 768-dimensional output are not checked against the released file. The paper itself gives both 1 and 32 attention heads.
The paper reports training on four RTX 3090 GPUs with 24 GB each. Memory and hardware needs for inference are not stated beyond the README's GPU requirement.
The README does not show how to turn the hidden states into task predictions, and the fine-tuning heads described in the paper are not part of the files read.

run_guide.summary: Get the DGRNA code at a pinned commit, place the downloaded checkpoint where the loader expects it, and run the README example to get hidden states for three RNA sequences.
prerequisites: A CUDA GPU. The README says only GPU is supported; GPU type and memory are not stated.
The packages the README lists: triton 2.2.0, causal-conv1d 1.2.2.post1, mamba-ssm 2.2.2 and fairseq 0.12.2, with PyTorch. The README gives no install command or Python version.
The checkpoint file checkpoint_best_100M.pt, downloaded by hand from the README's Google Drive folder and placed in ~/.cache/torch/hub/checkpoints/. No licence is stated for it.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/TimothyChen225/DGRNA.git
cd DGRNA
git checkout --detach 9f3513f6d84b5c62829860a99672a23b5e73d1af
steps.explanation: The README gives no clone command; these lines get the repository at the commit this page was written from. The example imports the DGRNA folder, so run it from the repository root.

steps.title: Run the README example
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import DGRNA
import torch

device = torch.device("cuda:0")
model, alphabet, _ = DGRNA.mamba2_pretrained.rna_mamba2_L24()
model = model.to(device)

batch_converter = alphabet.get_batch_converter()
model.eval()


data = [
    ("RNA1", "GGGUGCGAUCAUACCAGCACUAAUGCCCUCCUGGGAAGUCCUCGUGUUGCACCCCU"),
    ("RNA2", "GGGUGUCGCUCAGUUGGUAGAGUGCUUGCCUGGCAUGCAAGAAACCUUGGUUCAAUCCCCAGCACUGCA"),
    ("RNA3", "CGAUUCNCGUUCCC--CCGCCUCCA"),
]
batch_labels, batch_strs, batch_tokens = batch_converter(data)
batch_tokens = batch_tokens.to(device)
with torch.no_grad():
    #with torch.cuda.device(batch_tokens.device):
        results = model(batch_tokens)
        print(results)
PY
steps.explanation: The README usage snippet, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It loads the checkpoint from the torch hub folder and prints the model output for three example RNA sequences.

outputs: A printed tensor of hidden states for the three sequences; the model's forward pass returns hidden states rather than logits.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The dependency install and the Google Drive download are manual; the sources give no commands for them.

If checkpoint_best_100M.pt is not in the torch hub checkpoints folder, the loader tries to download a file of the same name from the RNA-FM project server instead. Check that the DGRNA file is in place before running.
